# atomwrite

> Atomic file operations for LLM agents: one CLI with 47 subcommands, NDJSON on stdout and BLAKE3 checksums on every write

atomwrite is a Rust CLI for reading, writing, editing, searching and transforming files with atomic write guarantees. Every write uses tempfile, fsync, rename and a directory fsync. Every response is NDJSON with BLAKE3 checksums. It is built for LLM agents that need reliable, structured file operations without corruption risk. This is the expanded reference: `llms.txt` is the short index of the same contract.

## Release 0.1.37

- Current version is 0.1.37 (MSRV 1.90), pin `^0.1.37`, with 47 subcommands (the single source of truth is `atomwrite agent-surface`)
- No telemetry and no product environment variables: configuration comes from CLI flags, the workspace `.atomwrite.toml` and the global XDG `config.toml`
- New `config` verb: `config path|list|get|set|unset|doctor` over 37 keys, with `--scope global|workspace` required on `path`, `set` and `unset`
- `scratch init PATH` creates the staging directory `.atomwrite/scratch/` inside the workspace jail, so patches never go through the OS `/tmp`
- A failed run ends with exactly one terminal event carrying `ok:false`, `code`, `exit`, `error_class`, `retryable` and `suggestion`, and `match_count` is always present on match failures
- Global agent-native stdout shape: `--select`/`--fields`, `--filter` and `--limit` (long-only, there is no global `-n`), plus the stream flags `--sort-by`, `--dedupe`, `--aggregate`, `--join`, `--diff-against`, `--redact`, `--normalize-encoding`, `--truncate-content` and `--max-output-bytes`
- `--non-interactive`, `--confirm-side-effect` and `--allow-truncate` are new global flags, and `suggestion_lang` names the language of `suggestion`
- A cancelled run ends with the `cancelled` envelope, and `deadline_exceeded` separates the `--timeout-secs` deadline (exit 124) from a signal (exit 130 or 143)
- `edit-loop` is all-or-nothing: a pair with no match exits 65 with `MATCH_FAILED`, and `--partial` writes the matching pairs and exits 87
- Every summary that publishes `files_failed` publishes `partial: true` beside it, and six new summary schemas are available through `--print-schema`
- Fuzzy matching has a content ceiling, `[fuzzy].max_content_bytes` (256 MiB)
- `watch` is no longer in the default build: install with `--features watch`
- Earlier releases: 0.1.35 (large overwrite default-deny, `watch_summary`, `delete --plan`), 0.1.34 (one-shot fuzzy), 0.1.33 (runtime hang fix and one-pass fuzzy), 0.1.32 (docs.rs `doc_cfg` and multi-target), 0.1.30 (agent surface). The subcommand count grew from 41 at 0.1.29 to 47 at 0.1.37, and `CHANGELOG.md` has the exact series

## Installation

```bash
cargo install atomwrite --locked
```

- The default build has the features `core`, `ast`, `lang-rust`, `lang-ts` and `lang-py`, and `semantic-search` is always compiled
- `watch` is opt-in: `cargo install atomwrite --locked --features watch`, and the default binary answers `watch` with exit 78 and `CONFIG_INVALID`
- Slim build: `cargo build --release --no-default-features --features core`, where `outline` and `sparse outline` exit 78 with a rebuild hint
- Full build: `cargo build --release --features full`
- Parsers for 305 languages are NOT bundled: the tree-sitter parsers are downloaded on first use by `tree-sitter-language-pack` (honouring the proxy settings of the host) and cached on disk, so the install footprint stays small
- The first run of each language therefore needs the network, and `atomwrite doctor` publishes the check `grammar_cache` with how many of the 23 grammars the AST verbs can need are already cached, so the condition is known before the run
- A grammar that is missing and cannot be downloaded is exit 69 `GRAMMAR_UNAVAILABLE` with class `precondition_failed`, and never exit 255; re-run the same verb once the network is up and the pack caches the grammar
- A panic writes a local report file in the temporary directory and the CLI never transmits it

## Setup For The Examples

Set `WS` once to the absolute path of the workspace root. Every example below passes `--workspace "$WS"`, because the path jail is anchored on that value and a wrong `.` moves the whole jail silently. The examples assume a small workspace with `src/a.rs`, `src/b.rs`, `src/c.rs`, `config.toml`, `notes.txt`, `rules.yaml` and `img.png`.

```bash
WS=/absolute/path/to/workspace
HASH_A=$(atomwrite --workspace "$WS" hash src/a.rs | jaq -r .checksum)
```

## 47 Subcommands

### Core I/O
- `read` -- read files with metadata, checksum and optional content. `--format raw|ndjson` selects a byte stream or the NDJSON envelope, and `--head`, `--tail`, `--lines START:END` and `--grep` narrow the content. Example: `atomwrite --workspace "$WS" read --head 2 src/a.rs`
- `write` -- create or overwrite files atomically via stdin; large targets require `--ack-overwrite` (default-deny), and `--preserve-timestamps` keeps the source mtime. Example: `printf 'x\n' | atomwrite --workspace "$WS" write notes/new.txt`
- `edit` -- surgically edit by line number, text marker, or exact/fuzzy match; multi-pair `--old`/`--new` has a per-pair fuzzy cascade, `pair_results` and `--partial`; stage `--old-file`/`--new-file` under `.atomwrite/scratch/`. Example: `atomwrite --workspace "$WS" edit src/b.rs --old beta --new gamma`
- `delete` -- delete files with backup; plan-only via `--plan`, a directory needs `-r` even for a plan, and `--confirm`/`--yes`/`-y` are rejected. Example: `atomwrite --workspace "$WS" delete --plan tmp.txt`
- `copy` -- copy files or trees with checksum verification (reflink on APFS, btrfs and XFS). Example: `atomwrite --workspace "$WS" copy src/a.rs src/a_copy.rs`
- `move` -- move or rename files atomically (EXDEV copy-fallback). Example: `atomwrite --workspace "$WS" move src/tmp.rs src/tmp2.rs`
- `apply` -- apply patches from stdin (unified diff, search/replace, full, markdown). Example: `printf 'new body\n' | atomwrite --workspace "$WS" apply --format full notes.txt`

### Search and replace
- `search` -- search file contents in parallel (ripgrep engine); `--no-begin-end` disables anchor emission. Example: `atomwrite --workspace "$WS" search alpha src/`
- `replace` -- replace text across files with atomic writes; `--fuzzy auto|aggressive|off` (`off` = exact-only, default `auto`) and `--fuzzy-threshold`; one-pass multi-apply on the original content (it never re-scans inserted text); default max applies is 1; if the replacement embeds the pattern it forces 1 apply; reports `strategy`, `similarity`, `match_count` and `indent_adjusted`; match errors may include `best_candidate`. Example: `atomwrite --workspace "$WS" replace --dry-run alpha omega src/`
- `transform` -- AST refactoring via ast-grep for the languages ast-grep supports (an unsupported language exits 65). Example: `atomwrite --workspace "$WS" transform --dry-run -p '$E.unwrap()' -r '$E?' -l rust src/`

### Inspection
- `hash` -- calculate BLAKE3 checksums. Example: `atomwrite --workspace "$WS" hash src/a.rs`
- `count` -- count lines and files by extension; `--by-size` lists the largest files. Example: `atomwrite --workspace "$WS" count --by-extension src/`
- `diff` -- compare two files (unified, stat or changes); `--algorithm myers|patience|lcs`. Example: `atomwrite --workspace "$WS" diff src/a.rs src/b.rs --unified`
- `list` -- list files in a directory tree. Example: `atomwrite --workspace "$WS" list --long --depth 1 src/`
- `extract` -- extract fields from NDJSON input via pipe (local `--field` or positionals; never `extract --select`, because the global `--select` only projects the emitted line). Example: `printf '{"a":1}\n' | atomwrite extract --field a`
- `extract-artifact` -- bounded signal from PDF, OOXML and image headers (never raw artifact bytes). Example: `atomwrite --workspace "$WS" extract-artifact img.png`
- `scope` -- grammatical scoping (delete all comments, and so on); `--language rust` or the alias `--lang rust`. Example: `atomwrite --workspace "$WS" scope src/ --language rust --query comments --delete --dry-run`
- `regex` -- generate a regex from examples. Example: `atomwrite regex abc-12 xyz-99 id-7 --digits`
- `calc` -- math and unit conversions. Example: `atomwrite calc "2 hours to seconds"`
- `completions` -- generate shell completions (bash, zsh, fish, elvish, powershell); `--install` writes them to the XDG data directory. Example: `atomwrite completions bash`

### Backup and recovery
- `backup` -- create timestamped backups with BLAKE3 checksums. Example: `atomwrite --workspace "$WS" backup src/a.rs --retention 3`
- `rollback` -- restore from a previous backup. Example: `atomwrite --workspace "$WS" rollback src/a.rs --latest --verify`
- `batch` -- NDJSON-driven batch operations (transactional with `--transaction`, which locks every target in path order before the snapshot). Example: `printf '{"op":"write","target":"batch.txt","content":"x"}\n' | atomwrite --workspace "$WS" batch --transaction`

### Batch helpers
- `edit-loop` -- N edits in 1 invocation via JSON array or NDJSON stdin (all-or-nothing: a pair with no match exits 65; `--partial` writes the matches and exits 87; the checksum read under the lock becomes the write base, so a concurrent edit exits 82). Example: `printf '[{"old":"gamma","new":"delta"}]\n' | atomwrite --workspace "$WS" edit-loop src/b.rs`
- `prune-backups` -- manual cleanup of legacy `.bak.*` files with `--max-age-secs` and `--max-count`. Example: `atomwrite --workspace "$WS" prune-backups --max-age-secs 86400 --dry-run .`

### WAL diagnostics
- `wal-stats` -- snapshot of the WAL journal state (counts, ages, sizes). Example: `atomwrite --workspace "$WS" wal-stats`
- `wal-heal` -- remove orphan terminal journals older than a threshold, and also remove a `Started` journal whose owning PID is gone, reported as `dead_owner_removed`; the path is required. Example: `atomwrite --workspace "$WS" wal-heal --threshold-secs 3600 .`

### Verification
- `verify` -- verify the BLAKE3 checksum of a file (exit 0 on match, 81 on mismatch), with the usage `verify <PATH> <HASH>`. Example: `atomwrite --workspace "$WS" verify src/a.rs "$HASH_A"`

### Structured config editors
- `set <PATH> <KEY_PATH> <VALUE>` -- write a value at a dotted path in a TOML or JSON file; preserves comments and key order via `toml_edit` and auto-coerces int, bool, float and string. Example: `atomwrite --workspace "$WS" set config.toml package.name demo2`
- `get <PATH> <KEY_PATH>` -- read a value at a dotted path; NDJSON `{"type":"get","key_path","value","found","format"}`. Example: `atomwrite --workspace "$WS" get config.toml package.name`
- `del <PATH> <KEY_PATH>` -- remove a key; `--force-missing` treats a missing key as a no-op success. Example: `atomwrite --workspace "$WS" del config.toml features.x`
- `case <PATHS...> --subvert OLD NEW --to <style>` -- rename identifiers across files via `heck`; styles are `snake`, `camel`, `pascal`, `kebab` and `screaming-snake`. It accepts files only: a directory exits 0 and changes nothing. Example: `atomwrite --workspace "$WS" case --subvert user_id UserId --to pascal --dry-run src/c.rs`

### AST tools
- `query` -- walk a tree-sitter AST and emit nodes as NDJSON (305 languages in `tree-sitter-language-pack`), with the usage `query <PATH> [--kinds|--query <KIND>|-Q <KIND>|--tree] [--positions]`. Example: `atomwrite --workspace "$WS" query --kinds src/a.rs`
- `outline <PATH> [--kind <KIND>] [--positions]` -- extract the high-level structure (functions, classes, structs, enums, traits, modules) of one file as NDJSON. Example: `atomwrite --workspace "$WS" outline src/a.rs`
- `write --syntax-check` runs a real tree-sitter syntax check for 24 languages and exits 88 with the first error line, column, kind and message

### Agent surface and workflows
- `recipe` -- list and run versioned multi-step pipelines such as search, replace and hash; `recipe run` needs `--path` or `--target`. Example: `atomwrite --workspace "$WS" recipe run --name search-replace-verify --pattern alpha --replacement omega --path src --dry-run`
- `sparse` -- budgeted monorepo list, read and outline (outline emits real AST `outline_item` events). Example: `atomwrite --workspace "$WS" sparse list src/ --max-files 10 --max-bytes 1048576`
- `semantic-merge` -- line-based three-way merge for multi-agent conflicts (not AST); markers are on by default and a conflict exits 84. Example: `atomwrite --workspace "$WS" semantic-merge --base base.txt --ours ours.txt --theirs theirs.txt --output merged.txt --fail-on-conflict`
- `agent-surface` -- clap-derived tool manifest (CLI only; integration is by subprocess with NDJSON output). Example: `atomwrite agent-surface --format json`
- `watch` -- filesystem events with debounce, checksum and gitignore options; always ends with a `watch_summary` NDJSON line; needs a build with `--features watch`, and the default binary exits 78 with `CONFIG_INVALID`. Example: `atomwrite --workspace "$WS" watch src/ --max-events 1 --idle-exit-ms 500`
- `codemod` -- multi-rule AST campaign with a `by_rule_id` summary, driven by a YAML rules file (format below). Example: `atomwrite --workspace "$WS" codemod --rules rules.yaml --dry-run src/`
- `semantic-search` -- offline token ranking over an inverted index (always compiled; not embeddings). Example: `atomwrite --workspace "$WS" semantic-search "unwrap value" src/ --k 5 --min-score 0.01`
- `stat` -- alias of `read --stat`. Example: `atomwrite --workspace "$WS" stat src/a.rs`
- `doctor` -- host readiness diagnostics (workspace, config, features, concurrency); `--strict` exits 1 with `DOCTOR_CHECKS_FAILED` on a failed check. Example: `atomwrite --workspace "$WS" doctor`
- `locale` -- show the resolved UI locale; `--set` and `--clear` manage the XDG preference. Example: `atomwrite locale`
- `commands` -- the full clap command tree as JSON for agent discovery (`--include-globals` adds the 33 global flags). Example: `atomwrite commands --include-globals`
- `scratch` -- `scratch init PATH` creates the staging directory inside the workspace (never the OS `/tmp`). Example: `atomwrite --workspace "$WS" scratch init .atomwrite/scratch`
- `config` -- persistent tuning keys: `config path|list|get|set|unset|doctor` over 37 keys of the XDG `config.toml` and the workspace `.atomwrite.toml`; atomic write, envelope `type:"config"`. Example: `atomwrite --workspace "$WS" config get fuzzy.threshold`

### Write durability
- `write --durability full|fast|auto` sets the fsync trade-off, and the NDJSON reports `platform.durability`, `platform.rename_method` and `platform.backup_method`
- Linux uses `renameat2` when available and falls back to rename
- macOS uses `F_FULLFSYNC` under durability `full`

## Write Safety Flags

These flags guard destructive writes. All of them are opt-in except the large-overwrite and shrink guards, which are on by default.

- `--ack-overwrite` -- required to overwrite an existing target above `[write].confirm_large_bytes` (default 100 KiB); without it the write exits 65
- `--allow-shrink` -- required when the new content is more than 50% smaller than the target
- `--require-backup` -- takes no value; aborts when a backup would not be made while the target exists
- `--auto-rotate` -- takes no value; forces backup rotation for recently modified targets
- `--risk-threshold <PERCENT>` -- warns when the size delta passes the percent; the default is 255, which means off, and a value such as 50 turns it on
- `--confirm` on `write` is a legacy alias with no effect, and `edit` has no confirmation flag, so use `--dry-run` first
- `delete --confirm`, `--yes` and `-y` are rejected: use `delete --plan` to preview and omit the flags to run
- `--expect-checksum <HASH>` -- optimistic locking: the comparison runs under the lock and a mismatch exits 82 `STATE_DRIFT`, while exit 81 `CHECKSUM_VERIFY_FAILED` belongs to `verify` and `read`
- `--locale <en|pt-BR>` -- display locale override, renamed from `--lang` in 0.1.20 to avoid clashing with the language selector of `scope` and `transform`

## Backups And Sequential Edits

- A single `BackupOpts` set (`--backup`, `--no-backup`, `--keep-backup`, `--retention <N>`) is shared by 15 mutating subcommands: `write`, `edit`, `edit-loop`, `replace`, `transform`, `scope`, `apply`, `set`, `del`, `case`, `batch`, `delete`, `move`, `copy` and `rollback`
- Backup is on by default: the backup is deleted after a successful write, kept when the write fails, and kept after success only with `--keep-backup`
- `delete` always keeps its backup, so `--keep-backup` on `delete` only adds a `warnings` field
- `--backup` and `--no-backup` are mutually exclusive (exit 2)
- `move` and `copy` overwrite an existing destination only with `--force` or an explicit `--backup`
- The `[defaults]` keys `backup` and `retention` of `.atomwrite.toml` apply to all 15 subcommands, with the precedence flags, then `.atomwrite.toml`, then the global `config.toml`, then the built-in default (`true` and `5`)
- `edit --allow-sequential-drift` suppresses `STATE_DRIFT` (exit 82) in a sequential pipeline and logs a warning
- Pattern A is to re-capture `checksum_after` after each `edit`, which has zero drift risk and is the right choice for concurrent agents
- Pattern B is to pass `--allow-sequential-drift` on every call, which needs fewer invocations but must never be used in a truly parallel scenario

## Output Contract

Every command writes NDJSON (one JSON object per line) to stdout, and stderr carries logs only. Query commands end with a summary event and write commands end with their own result event, so read the `type` of the last line. Schema files are in `docs/schemas/` (54 files serving 55 names, with `read` and `stat` sharing one; `atomwrite --print-schema` lists the 55 names). The contract is stable within the 0.1.x series. `--json` is accepted and ignored.

### Critical NDJSON fields
- `type` -- operation name (`set`, `get`, `del`, `case`, `query_match`, `outline_item`, `write`, `edit`, and so on)
- `ok` -- true on every success envelope, false on the terminal event of a failed run
- `checksum` (BLAKE3) -- the file content hash exposed by `read`, `write` and `hash`
- `checksum_before` and `checksum_after` (BLAKE3) -- exposed by `edit`: the hash before and after the operation
- `mtime_preserved` -- true if the mtime was kept, false if it was updated
- `bytes_written` -- total bytes written to the file
- `elapsed_ms` -- wall-clock time of the operation
- `target_resolved` and `target_source` -- the path that ran and where it came from: `argv` when the invocation line named it, `workspace` when an idempotent read verb fell back to the root, and `stdin` for the `-` operand
- `workspace_source` -- `argv` when the run got its root from `--workspace`, and `cwd` when it took the process working directory, so the ambient authority is visible

### Error envelope
- A failed run ends with exactly one terminal event: `{"error":true,"ok":false,"code":"...","exit":N,"message":"...","error_class":"permanent|transient|conflict|precondition_failed","retryable":false,"suggestion":"...","suggestion_lang":"en"}`
- `MATCH_FAILED` and `MATCH_AMBIGUOUS` (exit 65) add `best_candidate` and `match_count`
- Other optional fields are `missing_flag`, `conflict_count`, `pairs_total`, `pair_results`, `failed_pair_index`, `similar_paths` and `workspace`
- A cancelled run ends with `{"type":"cancelled","reason":"...","signal":"SIGTERM","deadline_exceeded":false}` and exit 124, 130 or 143
- Read the exit code before the stdout, retry only when `retryable` is true, and follow `suggestion`
- Under `--select`, `--filter` and `--limit` the envelope of an `ok:false` failure is never hidden
- Every verb that walks a tree reports files it could not read or write in `files_failed`, `partial` and `errors[]` (at most `summary.errors_max_entries` entries (50 by default), and `path` is the marker `<walk>` when the walk failed without naming a file of its own): `search`, `replace`, `transform`, `case`, `scope`, `sparse`, `semantic-search` and `backup` keep exit 0 when they answered and some file failed, while `count`, `list`, `hash`, `copy`, `delete` and `prune-backups` fail the run over a partial tree, and a run with no match and a failure exits with the first failure (the contract is ADR-0077, `docs/decisions/0077-answer-family-and-walk-honesty.md`)
- `print-schema` names an error contract too: `atomwrite --print-schema error`

## Local Flags

- `--expect-checksum <HASH>` -- optimistic locking for concurrent edits
- `--include <PATTERN>` / `-g <PATTERN>` -- filter files by glob pattern
- `--stat` (read) -- skip the file content, metadata only
- `--format raw|ndjson` (read) -- select a byte stream or the NDJSON envelope
- `--grep <REGEX>` (read) -- return only lines matching a regex
- `--head N` / `--tail N` (read) -- first or last N lines
- `--lines START:END` (read) -- partial read with a 1-based inclusive range
- `--by-size` (count) -- list the largest files
- `--no-begin-end` (search) -- disable anchor emission
- `--preserve-timestamps` (edit, replace, write) -- keep the original file mtime
- `--syntax-check` (write) -- real tree-sitter syntax check before commit
- `--positions` (query, outline) -- include `start_line`, `start_column` and `byte_offset`
- `--line-ending lf|crlf|cr|auto` (write) -- normalize line endings
- `--file <PATH>` (batch) -- read the NDJSON manifest from a file
- `--output-dir <DIR>` (backup) -- place backups in a custom directory
- `--install` (completions) -- install to the XDG data directory
- Advisory lock (automatic, no flag) -- `std::fs::File::try_lock` on the hidden `.<target>.atomwrite.lock` sidecar, which is `flock` on Unix and `LockFileEx` on Windows, 5 s wait, exit 83 on timeout
- A target name long enough to push the sidecar past 255 bytes gets a short BLAKE3 digest as the sidecar name, so the lock is taken instead of failing with `ENAMETOOLONG`

## Global Flags

There are 33 global flags (`atomwrite commands --include-globals` prints them). `--print-schema` must come before the command name.

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--workspace <DIR>` | current directory | workspace root of the path jail, required for file operations |
| `--config <PATH>` | none | explicit `.atomwrite.toml` path, fails if missing or malformed |
| `--locale <en\|pt-BR>` | system | display locale override |
| `-v` / `-vv` / `-vvv` | off | info, debug and trace logs on stderr |
| `-q` / `-qq` | off | error-only and silent logs |
| `--color auto\|always\|never` | `auto` | colored output control |
| `--no-color` | off | disable colored output |
| `--ready-file <PATH>` | none | write the PID after the signal handlers are ready (test harness only) |
| `--no-gitignore` | off | do not respect `.gitignore` files |
| `--hidden` | off | include hidden files and directories |
| `--follow-symlinks` | off | follow symbolic links |
| `-j` / `--threads <N>` | automatic | worker bound (alias `--max-concurrency`): 0 or omitted is the smaller of the logical CPUs, 16 and the RAM cap, and an explicit N is honoured even above 16 |
| `--max-filesize <BYTES>` | 1 GiB | reject files larger than N bytes (`search` has its own local limit that skips) |
| `--timeout-secs <N>` | 120 | global deadline (alias `--timeout`), `0` disables, exit 124 on expiry |
| `--no-progress` | off | suppress NDJSON progress heartbeats |
| `--json-schema` | off | print the JSON Schema of the subcommand output and exit |
| `--print-schema [NAME]` | none | list the 55 schema names or emit one, an unknown name exits 65 |
| `--non-interactive` | off | declare agent execution: never prompt, never read a confirmation from stdin |
| `--confirm-side-effect` | off | acknowledge a side effect where the command contract asks for it |
| `--allow-truncate` | off | opt in to value truncation, required by `--max-output-bytes` |
| `--no-auto-heal` | off | skip the startup wal-heal pass (threshold 3600 s, budget 100 ms) |
| `--select KEYS` / `--fields KEYS` | none | project NDJSON to top-level keys (CSV) |
| `--filter key=value` | none | keep events by top-level equality (repeatable AND, also `!=`) |
| `--limit N` | none | work budget: the target list is cut before the side effect and the walk stops at the record that reaches the cap, so `--limit 1` touches exactly ONE target and at most N answer records leave; and the terminal summary carries `walker_stopped_early: true` only when the walk was actually cut before the tree ended (long-only, `-n` belongs to `replace`) |
| `--sort-by path-line\|line-path\|KEY` | none | order buffered events |
| `--dedupe KEYS` | none | drop events whose key tuple was already seen |
| `--aggregate KEY[:OP[:FIELD]]` | none | group and reduce, OP is `count`, `sum`, `min` or `max` |
| `--join KEY:SUFFIX` | none | join the NDJSON table read from stdin into each event |
| `--truncate-content KEY:LEN` | none | truncate a string key to LEN characters |
| `--redact` | off | replace secret-shaped values with `[redacted]` |
| `--normalize-encoding` | off | normalize string values to Unicode NFC |
| `--diff-against PATH` | none | report added, removed and unchanged lines against a baseline NDJSON file (emits one `stream_diff` line) |
| `--max-output-bytes N` | none | cap every string value, `checksum` included, and requires `--allow-truncate` (each is rejected without the other, exit 2) |

## Configuration

`atomwrite config list` shows the 37 persistent keys with `value`, `origin` (`default`, `global` or `workspace`) and `default`. The global scope is the XDG `config.toml` (mode 0600) and the workspace scope is `.atomwrite.toml` at the workspace root. A flag still wins over both, and the two files are merged key by key.

| Key | Kind | Default | Scopes | Range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fuzzy.mode` | string | `auto` | global, workspace | `auto`, `aggressive`, `off` |
| `fuzzy.threshold` | float | 0.7 | global, workspace | 0.0 to 1.0 |
| `fuzzy.threshold_aggressive` | float | 0.5 | global, workspace | 0.0 to 1.0 |
| `fuzzy.threshold_context` | float | 0.8 | global, workspace | 0.0 to 1.0 |
| `fuzzy.threshold_jw` | float | 0.85 | global, workspace | 0.0 to 1.0 |
| `fuzzy.soft_floor_delta` | float | 0.05 | global, workspace | 0.0 to 1.0 |
| `fuzzy.max_content_bytes` | integer | 268435456 | global, workspace | bytes |
| `write.confirm_large_bytes` | integer | 102400 | global, workspace | bytes |
| `log.file` | boolean | false | global, workspace | true or false |
| `log.rotation` | string | `daily` | global, workspace | `daily` or `hourly` |
| `storage.home` | string | unset | global | a path |
| `locale` | string | unset | global | `en` or `pt-BR` |
| `concurrency.max_threads` | integer | 16 | global, workspace | 1 to 256 |
| `concurrency.ram_fraction_percent` | integer | 50 | global, workspace | 1 to 100 |
| `search.max_inflight_bytes` | integer | 8388608 | global, workspace | 4 MiB to 1 GiB |
| `lock.acquire_timeout_ms` | integer | 5000 | global, workspace | 100 to 3600000 |
| `retry.base_ms` | integer | 50 | global, workspace | 1 to 60000, not above `retry.max_ms` |
| `retry.max_ms` | integer | 400 | global, workspace | 1 to 60000 |
| `retry.max_elapsed_ms` | integer | 2000 | global, workspace | 1 to 3600000 |
| `extract.max_sample_rows` | integer | 10 | global, workspace | up to 100000 |
| `extract.max_text_chars` | integer | 400 | global, workspace | up to 10000000 |
| `extract.max_sheets` | integer | 32 | global, workspace | up to 10000 |
| `extract.max_slides` | integer | 64 | global, workspace | up to 10000 |

- Precedence: flags, then the workspace `.atomwrite.toml`, then the global `config.toml`, then the built-in defaults
- `config set KEY VALUE --scope global|workspace`, `config unset KEY --scope ...` and `config path --scope ...` need `--scope` (without it the exit is 2 and nothing is touched), while `config list` and `config get KEY` do not accept it
- `storage.home` and `locale` are global only: the workspace scope exits 65, while `log.file` and `log.rotation` are accepted in both scopes
- An unknown key or a value out of range exits 65 and writes nothing, while an unknown key or an invalid file inside a `config.toml` exits 78
- `set` keeps the comments of the file, validates the whole file and lands through tempfile, fsync and rename without a backup
- `config` works with a broken `config.toml`, and a file that is not valid TOML is never rewritten (`set` and `unset` exit 78)
- `defaults.line_ending`, `defaults.backup`, `defaults.retention` and `defaults.max_filesize` are `config` keys in both scopes, and the loader reads them from the same table
- Example: `atomwrite --workspace "$WS" config set fuzzy.threshold 0.9 --scope workspace`

## Codemod Rules File

`codemod --rules rules.yaml` takes a YAML list. Each rule has `language`, `pattern` and `rewrite`, and an optional `id` that tags the events and the `by_rule_id` summary.

```yaml
- id: unwrap-to-try
  language: rust
  pattern: '$E.unwrap()'
  rewrite: '$E?'
```

- `$NAME` matches one node and `$$$ARGS` matches several
- Run `codemod --dry-run` before you apply, and the same list works as `transform --rules rules.yaml`

## Exit Codes

The manifest of `atomwrite agent-surface --format json` lists 41 entries with 33 distinct exit numbers, and some numbers carry more than one `code`.

| Exit | Code | error_class | retryable |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `SUCCESS` | none | no |
| 1 | `NO_MATCHES` (zero results) | permanent | no |
| 1 | `DOCTOR_CHECKS_FAILED` (`doctor --strict`) | precondition_failed | no |
| 2 | `ARGUMENT_PARSE_ERROR` | permanent | no |
| 2 | `UNSUPPORTED_COMBINATION` (flags that cannot run together) | permanent | no |
| 4 | `FILE_NOT_FOUND` | permanent | no |
| 4 | `GLOB_NO_MATCHES` (a glob operand matched nothing) | permanent | no |
| 13 | `PERMISSION_DENIED` | permanent | no |
| 28 | `DISK_FULL` | transient | yes |
| 30 | `QUOTA_EXCEEDED` | transient | yes |
| 65 | `INVALID_INPUT` | permanent | no |
| 65 | `MATCH_FAILED` (with `best_candidate`, also an `edit-loop` pair with no match) | permanent | no |
| 65 | `MATCH_AMBIGUOUS` (with `best_candidate`) | permanent | no |
| 65 | `BINARY_FILE` | precondition_failed | no |
| 65 | `FILE_TOO_LARGE` | precondition_failed | no |
| 69 | `GRAMMAR_UNAVAILABLE` (AST verb with no cached parser and no network) | precondition_failed | no |
| 73 | `CROSS_DEVICE` | conflict | yes |
| 74 | `IO_ERROR` | transient | yes |
| 78 | `CONFIG_INVALID` (unknown key, invalid file, newer `version`, or a verb whose feature is missing from the build) | permanent | no |
| 80 | `TRANSACTION_ROLLBACK_FAILED` | permanent | no |
| 81 | `CHECKSUM_VERIFY_FAILED` | precondition_failed | no |
| 82 | `STATE_DRIFT` (optimistic locking failed) | conflict | yes |
| 83 | `LOCK_TIMEOUT` (automatic write lock, waits up to 5 s) | conflict | yes |
| 84 | `MERGE_CONFLICT` (semantic-merge) | permanent | no |
| 85 | `FIFO_DETECTED` | precondition_failed | no |
| 86 | `DEVICE_FILE` | precondition_failed | no |
| 87 | `EDIT_LOOP_PARTIAL` (`edit-loop --partial` wrote the matching pairs) | permanent | no |
| 88 | `SYNTAX_ERROR_DETECTED` | precondition_failed | no |
| 91 | `EXDEV_FALLBACK_DISABLED` | precondition_failed | no |
| 92 | `COPY_BACK_BLAKE3_FAILED` | conflict | yes |
| 93 | `ORPHAN_JOURNAL` | precondition_failed | no |
| 124 | `TIMEOUT` (global `--timeout-secs`, default 120, `0` disables) | precondition_failed | no |
| 126 | `WORKSPACE_JAIL` | precondition_failed | no |
| 127 | `SYMLINK_BLOCKED` | precondition_failed | no |
| 128 | `IMMUTABLE_FILE` | precondition_failed | no |
| 129 | `SIGHUP` | none | no |
| 130 | `CANCELLED` | permanent | no |
| 130 | `SIGINT` | none | no |
| 141 | `BROKEN_PIPE` (the reader closed the pipe, the output is incomplete) | permanent | no |
| 143 | `SIGTERM` (clean cancel, no tempfile left) | none | no |
| 255 | `INTERNAL_ERROR` | permanent | no |

- Exit 65 also covers a missing `--ack-overwrite`, a file above `[fuzzy].max_content_bytes` under fuzzy, an invalid regex or glob, an invalid AST pattern or rules file, and an invalid `config` key or value
- A run cancelled by SIGTERM, SIGINT or the deadline leaves no WAL journal, while a crash (`kill -9`) still leaves one and `wal-heal` is the recovery

## Upgrading To 0.1.37

`read` now accepts several targets, and this is additive for every caller that named one path.

- `read --format raw a.rs b.rs` and `read --format raw '*.rs'` concatenate byte for byte, exactly as `cat` does, with no header, no separator and no newline of its own
- Explicit paths are read in argv order, and a pattern is expanded by the binary against one level of its own directory, in `LC_ALL=C` byte order, skipping hidden names
- The batch copies in 64 KiB blocks and checks `--max-filesize` per target, so memory stays flat instead of holding the sum of the files
- A target that fails prints one line on stderr and the run continues, and the final status is the semantic code of the first failure (4 missing, 13 permission, 126 outside the `--workspace`), where `cat` would answer 1
- A `read --format raw` error now goes to stderr and never to stdout, because that channel promised bytes
- `--lines`, `--line`, `--context`, `--head`, `--tail`, `--grep`, `--stat` and `--verify-checksum` require a single target and exit 65 with more than one, and `read` with several targets without `--format raw` also exits 65
- A pattern with `**` or with more than one separator exits 65 with its own message instead of matching something else in silence
- One target in `--format raw` and the default NDJSON format are byte-identical to 0.1.37
- The copy advances the cancel check per block, so `--timeout-secs` cuts a batch with exit 124


## Upgrading To 0.1.37

These changes can break a consumer of the 0.1.36 contract.

- `watch` left the default feature set: the default binary exits 78 with `CONFIG_INVALID`, and `agent-surface` reports `available: false` with the install hint
- `edit-loop` is all-or-nothing: exit 65 means nothing was written, and `--partial` exits 87
- A failing summary (`search`, `replace`, `transform`, `edit-loop`, `semantic-merge`, `recipe`, `scope`) is the only error line of the run, and no second error envelope follows
- `apply` with a unified diff compares the context and the removed lines (shift up to 64 lines): a mismatch exits 65 `MATCH_FAILED` with `best_candidate` and writes nothing, where it used to write wrongly with exit 0
- `semantic-merge` with a conflict exits 84 `MERGE_CONFLICT`, not 65
- `case`, `transform`, `scope` and `codemod` fail a file that changed since it was read with `STATE_DRIFT` (82), so rerun the command
- A missing pair in `edit-loop` or in a multi-pair `edit` reports `MATCH_FAILED` instead of `INVALID_INPUT`
- An invalid regex or glob in any verb exits 65, not 255, and `doctor --strict` with a failed check exits 1, not 255
- `get`, `set` and `del` on an invalid TOML or JSON file exit 65, not 1
- `--max-output-bytes` requires `--allow-truncate`, and `null` fields are no longer emitted
- A block missing between similar lines under fuzzy is `MATCH_FAILED` and not `MATCH_AMBIGUOUS`
- `search.max_inflight_bytes` has a 4 MiB minimum, and a `.atomwrite.toml` that sets 1 MiB is rejected
- An unknown key or an invalid file in `config.toml` or `.atomwrite.toml` exits 78
- `replace`, `scope`, `codemod`, `case`, `delete`, `backup` and `prune-backups` need their paths, `wal-heal` and `scratch init` take the path as a positional, and `recipe run` needs `--path` or `--target`
- `--print-schema` must come before the command name, and an unknown name exits 65 with an error envelope
- `doctor` reads no environment variable and the `ci`, `github_actions` and `sudo` fields are gone from its report
- Full details and the step-by-step list are in `docs/MIGRATION.md`

## Environment, Signals And Privacy

- There are no product environment variables: use CLI flags, the global XDG `config.toml` and the workspace `.atomwrite.toml` only
- `doctor` reads no environment variable: host detection uses file probes only
- The CLI has no telemetry and never sends data anywhere
- The parser download is the only network use, it happens on the first use of an AST verb, and it honours the proxy settings of the host
- A panic writes a local report file in the temporary directory through `human-panic`, and nothing is transmitted
- SIGPIPE is handled by a cooperative handler instead of the default signal action: the process cleans up (no lock, journal or tempfile stays) and exits 141, so recheck the state instead of assuming the work finished
- SIGTERM exits 143, SIGINT 130, SIGHUP 129 and the deadline 124, each after a clean shutdown
- The production code has 8 `unsafe` blocks, in `signal.rs`, `platform.rs` and `signal_handlers.inc.rs`

## Usage Examples

Every block below was run against a fresh workspace. The expected exit code is 0 unless the comment says otherwise.

```bash
# Write atomically with checksum
printf 'content\n' | atomwrite --workspace "$WS" write src/file.rs
```

```bash
# Write with mtime preservation
printf 'content\n' | atomwrite --workspace "$WS" write --preserve-timestamps src/file.rs
```

```bash
# Read with checksum
atomwrite --workspace "$WS" read src/file.rs
```

```bash
# Read raw bytes (no envelope)
atomwrite --workspace "$WS" read --format raw src/file.rs
```

```bash
# Optimistic locking: only write if the file has not changed
CS=$(atomwrite --workspace "$WS" read src/file.rs | jaq -r .checksum)
printf 'new_value\n' | atomwrite --workspace "$WS" write --expect-checksum "$CS" src/file.rs
```

```bash
# Safety flags: require a backup and warn above a 50 percent size delta
printf 'new_value\n' | atomwrite --workspace "$WS" write --require-backup --risk-threshold 50 src/file.rs
```

```bash
# Overwrite a target above the large-file threshold (a rewrite that shrinks the file by more than 50 percent also needs --allow-shrink)
printf 'new_value\n' | atomwrite --workspace "$WS" write --ack-overwrite src/file.rs
```

```bash
# Search in parallel
atomwrite --workspace "$WS" search 'unwrap' src/ --include '*.rs'
```

```bash
# Count the largest files
atomwrite --workspace "$WS" count --by-size --top 10 src/
```

```bash
# Edit with match_count and the new checksum
atomwrite --workspace "$WS" edit src/c.rs --old user_id --new account_id --replace-all --fuzzy auto | jaq '{match_count,indent_adjusted,checksum_after}'
```

```bash
# edit-loop --partial: the second pair misses, the first is written and the exit code is 87
printf '[{"old":"account_id","new":"user_id"},{"old":"nothing_here","new":"x"}]\n' | atomwrite --workspace "$WS" edit-loop --partial src/c.rs
```

```bash
# Stage a patch inside the jail, then edit
atomwrite --workspace "$WS" scratch init .atomwrite/scratch
SCR="$WS/.atomwrite/scratch"
printf %s 'user_id' >"$SCR/old.txt"
printf %s 'owner_id' >"$SCR/new.txt"
atomwrite --workspace "$WS" edit --old-file "$SCR/old.txt" --new-file "$SCR/new.txt" src/c.rs
```

```bash
# Agent-native shape: a missing text exits 65 and the envelope keeps only the chosen keys
atomwrite --workspace "$WS" --select ok,error,code,match_count,suggestion --filter ok=false --limit 1 edit --old missing --new x --fuzzy off src/b.rs
```

```bash
# Replace across files: preview first, then apply
atomwrite --workspace "$WS" replace --dry-run 'alpha' 'omega' src/
atomwrite --workspace "$WS" replace 'alpha' 'omega' src/
```

```bash
# AST transform via ast-grep
atomwrite --workspace "$WS" transform -p '$E.unwrap()' -r '$E?' -l rust src/
```

```bash
# Batch operations (transactional)
printf '{"op":"write","target":"batch.txt","content":"x"}\n' | atomwrite --workspace "$WS" batch --transaction
```

```bash
# Math, units and regex generation
atomwrite calc "2 GiB to bytes"
atomwrite regex "2024-01-15" "2025-12-31" "2026-07-04"
```

```bash
# Structured editors and case renaming
atomwrite --workspace "$WS" set config.toml package.version 0.2.0
atomwrite --workspace "$WS" get config.toml package.version
atomwrite --workspace "$WS" case --subvert user_id UserId --to pascal src/c.rs
```

```bash
# Walk the AST and read the outline
atomwrite --workspace "$WS" query --kinds src/a.rs
atomwrite --workspace "$WS" outline src/a.rs --kind function_item
```

```bash
# Real syntax check before commit
printf 'fn main() {}\n' | atomwrite --workspace "$WS" write --syntax-check src/parser.rs
```

```bash
# Backup, then roll back
atomwrite --workspace "$WS" backup src/a.rs
atomwrite --workspace "$WS" rollback src/a.rs --latest --verify
```

```bash
# Apply a unified diff from stdin
printf -- '--- a/notes.txt\n+++ b/notes.txt\n@@ -1,2 +1,2 @@\n-one\n+uno\n two\n' | atomwrite --workspace "$WS" apply notes.txt
```

```bash
# Plan a delete: a directory needs -r even for a plan
atomwrite --workspace "$WS" delete --plan -r src/
```

```bash
# Persistent tuning keys
atomwrite --workspace "$WS" config list
atomwrite --workspace "$WS" config set fuzzy.threshold 0.9 --scope workspace
```

```bash
# Agent discovery
atomwrite --workspace "$WS" doctor --strict
atomwrite commands --include-globals
atomwrite agent-surface --format json
atomwrite locale
```

```bash
# Codemod: preview the rules file above
atomwrite --workspace "$WS" codemod --rules rules.yaml --dry-run src/
```

```bash
# Stream shape: sort and count without jq
atomwrite --workspace "$WS" --sort-by path-line --aggregate type:count list src/ --depth 1
```

```bash
# Continuous watch with a ceiling: exits 78 on a build without the watch feature
atomwrite --workspace "$WS" watch src/ --max-events 100 --idle-exit-ms 500 --checksum
```
